correctness.rationale: For every prime power q and integer k>=2, each k-subspace U is carried by a linear stabilizer of A to C⊕D with dim C=s and dim D=k-s. Every complement W of A is a graph f:B→A. It avoids U exactly when the quotient restriction f|_D:D→A/C is invertible, giving |GL(k-s,q)|q^{s(k-s)+ks}=q^{k²}∏_{j=1}^{k-s}(1-q^{-j}); these strictly increase with s. The first refinement distinguishes A and N(A), and the second counts N(U)∩N(A). Stabilizer transitivity bounds refinement by orbit partition. Size counts q^{(k-s)²}[k s]_q² follow from independently choosing intersections and graph maps. Round1 has exactly three classes, proving 2-round sharpness k>=3. Actual standard-library scripts enumerate q2 k2, q3 k2, q2 k3 and test Möbius identities for 35 more configurations; none is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A structurally motivated, exact orbit-recovery theorem with a sharp constant depth for the full unbounded balanced subspace-Kneser graph family. The result recovers all k+1 intersection-orbit classes from a single marked vertex while 1-WL sees only three initial refinement classes; it produces an exact formula for their sizes. This is a precise logical-depth/orbit classification and not an unmotivated finite census, isolated computation, or a claim of general graph identification.
